title: Highest Volcanoes in the World
scope_note: What counts: volcanoes on the Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program's Holocene list (evidence of activity in the last ~11,700 years), ranked by the summit elevation GVP gives. Older, extinct volcanoes such as Kilimanjaro, Sajama and Tupungato (GVP's Pleistocene list) are not included. A volcano on a border is shown under the first country GVP lists for it, with a SHARED WITH badge. Other surveys can differ by tens of metres.

insights.text: No Kilimanjaro? GVP lists it as Pleistocene: no known eruption in the last 11,700 years.
From the seafloor up, Hawaii's Mauna Kea stands about 10,200 m: taller than all of these.
Chile flies 30 of these 50 flags, but 18 sit on its border with Argentina or Bolivia.
Next: Sabancaya, the highest volcano on this list that erupted in 2026.
Chimborazo is only #8 here, yet its summit is the farthest point from Earth's centre.
Both of the top two have erupted: Ojos del Salado around 750 CE, Llullaillaco in 1877.

layout.image_prefer: the whole volcano clearly visible and recognisable (snow-capped cone, summit crater, eruption plume or its classic landscape view), the correct named volcano and not a neighbouring peak, landscape or portrait both fine

items.name: Ojos del Salado
items.subtitle: Puna de Atacama, Andes
items.image_hint: Ojos del Salado volcano, the highest volcano on Earth (6,893 m) on the Chile-Argentina border near Paso San Francisco / Laguna Verde (Chile); broad desert massif with a rocky summit crater rim and small snow patches above brown-red Puna desert; classic view from the Chilean side (Laguna Verde, Atacama Refuge) or Argentinian side (Fiambala route). NOT Nevado Tres Cruces, NOT El Muerto, NOT Incahuasi, NOT Monte Pissis

source.name: Smithsonian GVP, Volcanoes of the World: Ojos del Salado, Nevados (355130)

items.name: Pico de Orizaba
items.subtitle: Puebla / Veracruz, Mexico
items.image_hint: Pico de Orizaba (Citlaltépetl), Mexico's highest mountain, Puebla / Veracruz: classic snow-capped symmetric cone, seen from the Puebla side (Tlachichuca, sunrise) or across farmland; clear sky. NOT Popocatépetl, NOT Iztaccíhuatl, NOT Sierra Negra

source.name: Smithsonian GVP, Volcanoes of the World: Orizaba, Pico de (341100)

items.notes: GVP Holocene list; GVP country field 'Mexico'; type Stratovolcano; last eruption 1846 (Eruption Observed). Wikipedia gives 5,636 m (+1.3%); ranking uses the GVP value throughout.

items.name: Isluga
items.subtitle: Tarapacá, Chile
items.image_hint: Isluga volcano (5,550 m), Volcán Isluga National Park, Tarapacá, Chile: snow-dusted volcanic cone with fumaroles, often seen behind the white adobe church of the Isluga village or the Enquelga wetlands with llamas. NOT Tata Sabaya

source.name: Smithsonian GVP, Volcanoes of the World: Isluga (355030)

items.notes: GVP Holocene list; GVP country field 'Chile'; type Stratovolcano; last eruption 1913 (Eruption Observed).

items.name: Yucamane
items.subtitle: Tacna, Peru
items.image_hint: Yucamane volcano (5,495 m), Tacna Region, southern Peru, near Candarave and Laguna Suches / Aricota: steep snow-capped symmetric cone. NOT Tutupaca, NOT El Misti

source.name: Smithsonian GVP, Volcanoes of the World: Yucamane (354050)

items.notes: GVP Holocene list; GVP country field 'Peru'; type Stratovolcano(es); last eruption -1320 (Eruption Observed).

items.name: Cordón del Azufre
items.subtitle: Atacama, Andes
items.image_hint: Cordón del Azufre volcanic chain (5,481 m) on the Chile-Argentina border next to Lastarria, Salta / Antofagasta: row of brown and ochre volcanic vents with sulphur, puna desert. NOT Volcán Azufre elsewhere

source.name: Smithsonian GVP, Volcanoes of the World: Cordon del Azufre (355121)

items.notes: GVP Holocene list; GVP country field 'Chile-Argentina'; type Complex; last eruption None (Evidence Credible).

items.name: Corrida de Cori
items.subtitle: Puna de Atacama, Andes
items.image_hint: Corrida de Cori volcanic field (5,451 m) on the Chile-Argentina border, Salta / Antofagasta, near Salar de Llullaillaco and Llullaillaco volcano: group of brown volcanic cones and lava flows in the high desert. NOT Llullaillaco itself

source.name: Smithsonian GVP, Volcanoes of the World: Corrida de Cori Volcanic Field (355112)

items.notes: GVP Holocene list; GVP country field 'Chile-Argentina'; type Stratovolcano; last eruption None (Evidence Uncertain).

items.name: Tata Sabaya
items.subtitle: Oruro, Bolivia
items.image_hint: Tata Sabaya volcano (5,430 m), Oruro Department, Bolivia, on the northern shore of Salar de Coipasa: snow-capped cone above the white salt flat. NOT Isluga, NOT Tunupa (Salar de Uyuni)

source.name: Smithsonian GVP, Volcanoes of the World: Tata Sabaya (355032)

items.notes: GVP Holocene list; GVP country field 'Bolivia'; type Stratovolcano; last eruption None (Evidence Credible).

items.name: Cerro Bayo
items.subtitle: Puna de Atacama, Andes
items.image_hint: Cerro Bayo / Bayo Gorbea volcanic complex (5,413 m), Chile-Argentina border near Lastarria and Cordón del Azufre (Salta / Antofagasta): pale yellowish-brown volcanic peaks in the high Puna. NOT other hills called Cerro Bayo (Villa La Angostura ski area, etc.)

source.name: Smithsonian GVP, Volcanoes of the World: Bayo Gorbea, Cerro (355122)

items.notes: GVP Holocene list; GVP country field 'Chile-Argentina'; type Complex; last eruption None (Evidence Credible).

items.name: Popocatépetl
items.subtitle: Puebla / Mexico State, Mexico
items.image_hint: Popocatépetl volcano, Mexico: snow-capped cone with an ash or steam plume, classic view from Paso de Cortés, Amecameca or behind the Iglesia de los Remedios in Cholula. NOT Iztaccíhuatl (the long ridge to its north), NOT Pico de Orizaba

source.name: Smithsonian GVP, Volcanoes of the World: Popocatepetl (341090)

items.notes: GVP Holocene list; GVP country field 'Mexico'; type Stratovolcano(es); last eruption 2026 (Eruption Observed). BOUNDARY: #51 is Ticsani (5382 m GVP), 11 m lower.
